issues.claim: Partly fixed: §8.8 now applies an Auto change decided while the view is idle at once, and a device-pixel-ratio change at once when idle (J-A121.07; T-ER-26), but §12.5 *The frame budgets Auto holds* still reads 'a rolling p95 over the budget through 2 s steps one rung … down, one under 60 % of it through 10 s one up, each applied only at the settle and at most once in 10 s'. *The settle* is §8.8's gesture event (*Gestures*: 'the settle, at which the Auto changes decided during the gesture apply'), so a builder reading §12.5 never applies a change decided on an idle view: VRC2T-08's defect, restated in the same unit.
issues.required_change: §12.5's clause reads '… each applied only while the view is settled — at once when no gesture runs, at the gesture's settle otherwise — and at most once in 10 s (§8.8's Auto loop) …'.

issues.claim: §11.2 *At a drawn week* (new this round): 'every row, count, match and gap unit is the head index's restricted to the entities the frame holds'. A kind chip's match is 'every entity holding an admitted Use whose cls is among its classes … one match per entity' (*Find's match listing*), and a Use is itself an addressed record with `opened`/`closed` (§2.6), while V06 §3.15.2's frame is a whole model with its own uses. So at a scrubbed week (a) a building that held a smithy then and a bakery at the head is matched by 'Bakery' (the building is held by the frame) and not by 'Smithy', glowing, pinning and counting a use the frame does not draw — unless 'entities' includes the Use, which two builders read two ways; (b) a use or building the frame holds that the head has since closed, moved or demolished is in no head row and is never matched though drawn — the second half of VRC2T-07's claim, left standing against R3-24's own sentence ('Find counts, glows, pins, lists and gaps only the entities that frame holds'). T-ER-25's scrub fixtures exercise neither case.
issues.required_change: §11.2 *At a drawn week* reads: 'where that week's frame is not the head, the listing is the frame's: the head index's matches less those whose entity, or whose matching use, the frame does not hold open at that week, plus the frame's own uses and entities of the chip's classes or target that the head lacks or holds otherwise — read from V06 §3.15.2's frame (its Use records with `opened` at or before the week and no `closed` by it; the HistoryStore images between the frame and the head) — so a building matches by its use at that week, never its head use, and an entity or use the frame holds matches though the head has since closed, moved or demolished it; a chip with none there counting 0; absent, the head'; §8.2's *At a drawn week* sentence cites it ('each chip's matches are §11.2's listing at that week'); T-ER-25's scrub fixture adds a week before a matched use closed and a building whose use changed since that week (matched by its use then; the closed use matched and drawn). V09 §4.21.10 (8) and V10's `read_map find` then read the same listing (their 'restricted to the entities that frame holds' citing §11.2).

issues.claim: R3-21 (a) rules the layers shown document style state — `LayerSpec.visible` set by a logged `setLayer`, never a `view.set` key — and §11.3 now says '`LayerSpec` is the document's style state, §8.4, and no view key, so `view.set` never carries it'. §2.9 *View state* still opens 'time, location, favourites, notes and public notes, view pins, layer choices, `stylePreset` …' (l. 3318), the per-viewer, unlogged state outside every digest. One builder makes the layers shown a per-viewer view key, another a logged, undoable, shared event (§7.1's T12 `dress`; §8.4).
issues.required_change: §2.9's *View state* list drops 'layer choices' and adds after the list: 'The layers shown are no view key: `LayerSpec.visible` is the document's style state, set by a logged `setLayer` (§8.4, §7.1; §11.3).'

issues.claim: T121-2 (§13.8, l. 18384–18386): 'no level change while a pan, zoom or drag is in progress — a change lands only at §8.8's settle —'. Under §8.8's rule as repaired (VRC2T-08; J-A121.07) a change decided while the view is idle lands at once, with no settle event, and T-ER-26's bar runs T121-2 with 'with the view idle the DPR change and the step-down each applied within one frame of the decision (T121-2, T121-7)'. The two bars disagree on the idle case; T121-2 as written fails a correct implementation.
issues.required_change: T121-2's dash clause reads '— a change lands only while the view is settled: at once when no gesture runs, at §8.8's settle after one —'.

issues.claim: T-V9-84 (V09 l. 4367): 'a device-pixel-ratio change re-evaluates within one frame and the level changes only at the next settle (T121-7)', unqualified, while §8.8 applies a DPR change 'at once while the view is idle, at the settle while a gesture runs' and T-ER-26 requires the idle change 'applied within one frame of the decision'. On an idle view T-V9-84 fails the design's behaviour or makes the builder wait for a gesture. (V09's edge row 89 and V12's edge row 32 speak of a change during a gesture and agree.)
issues.required_change: T-V9-84's clause reads 'a device-pixel-ratio change re-evaluates within one frame and the level changes at once when the view is idle, at the gesture's settle when one runs (§8.8; T121-7)'.

issues.claim: Partly fixed: §11.2's `interface ExportOpts` is declared once with `Format` and `ViewHandle`, and §14's `Exporter`, §11.1 and V08 W81 cite it; but it says it holds 'every option an export reads, declared once … written by V09 §5.10's dialog', while V09 §5.10 offers, and §11.1 / V02 §5.5 / V09 §5.15 define, options with no member: Map data's 'Raised ways' and 'Retaining walls' checkboxes (file f item 447 (a)) and 'include supply links' (V09 §5.15's `supplyLink` LineStrings); GeoJSON's optional `wings` layer (§11.1; V02 §5.5); 3-D's 'terrain, trees and lights on · off' (`trees` is typed for GeoJSON only); Tabletop's layer 'a raised way's deck' (`vtt.scene` has no raised-way form).
issues.required_change: `ExportOpts` gains, each with its default: `links?: boolean` (GeoJSON, V09 §5.15; default on while the view's `thematic` is `links`), `raised?: boolean` and `retaining?: boolean` (GeoJSON, file f item 447 (a); default true), `wings?: boolean` (GeoJSON, V02 §5.5; default false), `terrain?: boolean` and `lights?: boolean` (3-D; default true) with `trees` extended to the 3-D formats (`'none'` leaving them out, else drawn), and `vtt.scene` the form `{ raisedWay: Id }` (one deck scene, §11.1 *Per raised way*).

issues.claim: The new typed `ExportOpts` members state ranges a script or a bridged `export.request` can pass outside — `vtt.pxPerSquare` 'at least 50', `band` 'neighbourhood only for a district-sized or smaller frame', `vtt.scene` naming a building, storey or depth band, `stride` (years), `size` (`px`, `dpi`) — and nothing says what an export does with 30 px a square, the neighbourhood band over a whole town, a storey the building lacks, a stride of 0 or a zero-sized picture (clamp, refuse or draw); T-ER-19 and T-ER-20 test none. The dialog never produces such values (no normal path, hence minor).
issues.required_change: §11.2 states beside `ExportOpts`: a member outside its range that has a nearest lawful value is clamped to it and named in the export's report (`pxPerSquare` → 50; `band` 'neighbourhood' over a larger frame → 'district'); one with none — a `vtt.scene` naming what the scope lacks, a `stride` ≤ 0, a `size` side or `dpi` ≤ 0, a zero-area `frame` — refuses the export (`export.refused` / the rejected promise, naming the member), never a crash or a hang; T-ER-19 adds a request of each.

issues.claim: `ExportOpts.frame?: BoxCm` (new) and `thumbnail`'s `box: BoxCm` use `BoxCm`; `DisplayList.bounds: Box`, `dirty: Box[]`, `LiveLayerProvider.marks(…, region: Box)`, `VectorBackend`'s `frame: Box` (the writer `ExportOpts.frame` feeds) and §14's `ObstacleSource` use `Box`. Neither is declared anywhere in the set (principle (2): one name per concept).
issues.required_change: §8.1's code block declares `type Box = { x0: Cm; y0: Cm; x1: Cm; y1: Cm };   // an axis-aligned box in world cm, as MarkTable.bbox's four values`; §11.2's `ExportOpts.frame` and `thumbnail`'s `box` read `Box`.

issues.claim: §11.3: '`export.request` becomes `export.request { fmt, opts, displayNames?, knowledge?: Admission, bundle?: true }`', while `opts` is now §11.2's `ExportOpts`, whose members include `knowledge` and `displayNames`; §11.1 says 'the bridge's `export.request` carries the same field'. Two slots for one value, with no rule for which governs when both are sent.
issues.required_change: §11.3's message reads `export.request { fmt: Format, opts?: ExportOpts, bundle?: true }` — the requester's `knowledge` and `displayNames` being `opts`' members (§11.2) — and V08 §2.2's comment 'export.request gains displayNames?: …, knowledge?: Admission …' reads 'export.request's `opts` carries `displayNames` and `knowledge` (§11.2's `ExportOpts`)' (V08's end).
